tools.name: org_authenticate
tools.description: Verify an existing session token. Returns the authenticated user and organisation. Use this to confirm a stored token is still valid before making other API calls.

tools.name: org_refresh_token
tools.description: Refresh an existing session token, extending its validity for a full new lifetime (7 days by default). Rarely needed: tokens past half of their lifetime are refreshed automatically on any tool call. Use this only to force a refresh explicitly.

tools.name: org_register
tools.description: Register a new organisation and its first admin user. The default subscription plan is applied automatically.

name.description: Full name of the admin user

email.description: Email address of the admin user

orgName.description: Name of the organisation to create

tools.name: org_invite_member
tools.description: Invite a user to the organisation by email with a specified role

tools.name: org_accept_invite
tools.description: Accept an organisation invite using the invite token received by email

token.description: Invite token from the invitation email

name.description: Full name of the user accepting the invite

tools.name: org_request_otp
tools.description: Send a one-time password to the user's email address to start the login flow. Call org_verify_otp next with the code from the email.

tools.name: org_verify_otp
tools.description: Verify the one-time password and return session credentials. Store the returned token, userId, and orgId in ~/.syntica/credentials.json (outside the project, mode 0600 — write it with `umask 077`, never into the repository). If the response has pendingOrgSelection=true, the user belongs to multiple organisations: ask them which one to use and call org_select with the token and chosen orgId — do NOT persist the pending token as the session.

code.description: One-time password code from the email

tools.name: org_select
tools.description: Choose which organisation to use after login (when org_verify_otp returned pendingOrgSelection), or switch to a different organisation mid-session. Returns a fresh token scoped to that org. Store the returned token and orgId in ~/.syntica/credentials.json (outside the project, mode 0600), replacing any previous token/orgId.

token.description: Current token — the pending token from org_verify_otp, or an existing session token when switching orgs

orgId.description: ID of the organisation to switch to (from org_verify_otp orgs or org_list_orgs)

tools.name: org_list_orgs
tools.description: List the organisations the current user belongs to, with the one the current token is scoped to. Call this whenever the user mentions another organisation, asks what they have access to, or before creating an application when you have not confirmed which organisation they mean — a session token is scoped to ONE organisation, and working in another needs org_select, not a different orgId argument.

tools.name: app_list
tools.description: List all applications for an organisation.

tools.name: app_create
tools.description: Create a new application. Returns the application ID and git clone URL for pushing code. The application is created in the organisation the token is scoped to — if the user belongs to more than one (org_list_orgs), ask which one they mean before creating, and call org_select first if it is not the current one.

name.description: Application name — lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only

orgId.description: Organisation ID — must be the organisation this token is scoped to. To act in a different one, call org_select first; passing another org id here does not switch organisation.

templateId.description: Optional template ID from org_list_templates to scaffold the application

githubConnectionId.description: Optional: a GitHub-App-backed connection id (org_list_git_connections, appInstallation: true; connect one with org_connect_github). The platform then CREATES the source repository in that GitHub account, pushes the template scaffold into it, and binds it as the upstream — included on every plan. Requires templateId.

githubRepoName.description: Repository name to create on GitHub (with githubConnectionId). Defaults to the application name.

githubPrivate.description: Whether the created GitHub repository is private (default true).

cloudAccount.description: Optional cloud account (id or name from org_list_cloud_accounts) for the free dev environment: the Syntica account or a connected AWS account of the organisation whose stack is current. Leave it out unless the user names one.

tools.name: app_delete
tools.description: Delete an application together with every environment and instance it runs, and its data. The repository is moved to trash and can be restored with app_restore for about 30 days, but the deployed environments and their data are destroyed and cannot be restored. By default the delete happens now. Slots already paid for stay paid until the 1st and can be reused by a new application or environment until then, and the reply lists them. Pass when "period_end" to delete on the 1st instead, or an ISO-8601 time before the 1st. Needs an org admin. Destructive: confirm with the user before calling.

when.description: 'now' (default), 'period_end' (the 1st 00:00 UTC) or an ISO-8601 time before the 1st

tools.name: app_list_deleted
tools.description: List soft-deleted applications for an organisation (the restore view). Use this to find the applicationId to pass to app_restore, and to see how long is left before each is permanently purged.

tools.name: app_restore
tools.description: Restore a soft-deleted application within its recovery window. Find the applicationId with app_list_deleted first. Fails if the recovery window has elapsed (the app was already permanently purged).

applicationId.description: ID of the soft-deleted application (from app_list_deleted)

tools.name: app_rename
tools.description: Rename an application and its git repository. WARNING: this changes the repo path, so existing git clone/remote URLs (and the cloneUrl) stop working — anyone with a local clone must update their remote to the new cloneUrl returned here. The name must be lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only, and unique in the org.

name.description: New application name — lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only

tools.name: org_list_members
tools.description: List all members of an organisation and their roles

tools.name: org_list_plans
tools.description: List the available subscription plans (free and pay-as-you-go) from the Stripe catalog, with each plan's name and base price

tools.name: org_get_subscription
tools.description: Get the current subscription plan (free or pay-as-you-go) for an organisation

tools.name: org_get_billing
tools.description: Show the organisation's current bill: the plan, the monthly total Stripe will charge, and a per-line breakdown (node tiers, applications, environments, backups, traffic, add-ons) with quantities and amounts. Read-only — this does not change anything.

tools.name: org_setup_git_credentials
tools.description: Generate a long-lived git credential token for cloning and pushing repositories via HTTPS. Stores the token so git works from any terminal without re-authenticating. If an application deploys from your own repository (see app_set_upstream), these credentials are read-only for it — pushes to the platform-hosted repository are refused, and you should push to your own repository instead. NOT for connecting your own GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket repository — to store a credential for a host you own repositories on, use org_add_git_connection instead.

label.description: Label to identify this credential, e.g. "laptop" or "work" (default: "default")

tools.name: org_revoke_git_credentials
tools.description: Revoke a git credential token by its ID

credentialId.description: ID of the credential to revoke

tools.name: org_list_git_credentials
tools.description: List all git credentials for the authenticated user

tools.name: app_set_upstream
tools.description: Point an application at a git repository you host yourself, using a remote repository connection you have already created. Create that connection first with org_add_git_connection, and find its id with org_list_git_connections — the credential lives on the connection, so this call takes only the repository path within its host and the branch. WARNING: this is destructive to the platform-hosted repository. On the next deploy the platform force-fetches your repository over its mirror, so any commit that exists only in the platform-hosted repository is lost. Afterwards pushes to it are refused and templates can no longer be applied — push to your own repository instead. Returns the list of branches found in the repository.

connectionId.description: Remote repository connection id, from org_list_git_connections or org_add_git_connection. Supplies the host and the stored credential.

path.description: Repository path within the connection's host, e.g. "acme/api". Must not be a full URL — the host comes from the connection. A leading slash and a trailing ".git" are both optional.

branch.description: Branch to deploy from, e.g. main

tools.name: app_clear_upstream
tools.description: Disconnect an application from its own git repository and return it to a platform-hosted repository. The hosted repository becomes writable again (its history is kept). The stored access token remains in your organisation and can be removed with org_list_git_connections.

tools.name: org_list_git_connections
tools.description: List the git connections (stored access tokens for your own repositories) in an organisation. Credential material is never returned — only the provider, host, username, last-used/last-error status, and isDefault for the org's default GitHub account (change it with org_set_default_git_connection).

tools.name: org_set_default_git_connection
tools.description: Set or clear the organisation's default GitHub account (org admins only). New applications created from Claude in the browser or the web app land in the default account, so members without a GitHub account can still create and edit apps. Pass a connectionId from org_list_git_connections to make it the default: it must be a Syntica GitHub App installation (appInstallation: true) on a GitHub Organization, not a personal account. Omit connectionId to clear the default. At most one connection is the default; setting a new one replaces the old.

connectionId.description: The connection to make the default (org_list_git_connections). Omit it to clear the default.

tools.name: org_add_git_connection
tools.description: Add a remote repository: store a credential for a git host you own repositories on (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or any HTTPS git server), so applications can deploy from it. This is the paid external-source-repository feature. For GitHub, prefer org_connect_github (the Syntica GitHub App): one click, no token to manage, and included on every plan. NOT for the platform-hosted repository — for a token to clone or push that, use org_setup_git_credentials instead. One connection covers every repository on that host for that username, and applications are bound to it with app_set_upstream. Re-running this for the same host and username rotates the stored token rather than creating a duplicate. Credential material is never returned.

url.description: Any HTTPS URL on the host to connect, e.g. https://github.com or https://github.com/acme/api.git. Only the host is stored.

username.description: Git username. Omit for a public repository or a token-only credential. Provider-specific: a Bitbucket app password needs the Atlassian username, an Atlassian API token needs the account email address, and a repository/project access token needs no username at all.

accessToken.description: Read-scoped access token. Omit for a public repository.

label.description: Human-readable name for this connection. Defaults to the host.

provider.description: Inferred from the URL's host (github.com, gitlab.com, bitbucket.org) when omitted — pass this explicitly for an enterprise or self-hosted git server.

tools.name: org_connect_github
tools.description: Connect a GitHub account to the organisation via the Syntica GitHub App — no personal access token needed, and included on every plan. Returns an install URL the USER must open in their browser to approve the installation; once approved, the connection appears in org_list_git_connections with appInstallation: true. With such a connection, app_create can create the source repository in their GitHub account (githubConnectionId) so they can edit code on GitHub and deploy from it, and org_list_github_repos lists their existing repositories to deploy from instead. For a non-GitHub host, or to connect a pre-existing repository with a token, use org_add_git_connection instead (paid feature).

tools.name: org_list_github_repos
tools.description: List the repositories a GitHub App connection can reach (newest-pushed first, up to 100), so the user picks one instead of typing owner/repo. Use with a connection from org_list_git_connections that has appInstallation: true. To deploy from one of the listed repositories, call app_set_upstream with its fullName as the path and (usually) its defaultBranch — note that binding a pre-existing repository is the paid external-source-repository feature. Creating a NEW repository instead (app_create with githubConnectionId) is included on every plan. If a repository is missing here, the user limited the installation to selected repositories — they manage that on GitHub under Settings → Applications.

connectionId.description: A GitHub App connection id (appInstallation: true) from org_list_git_connections

tools.name: app_repo_tree
tools.description: List the file tree of an application's code, on its deploy branch. No GitHub credential is needed in this session. Call this before reading or saving, to see what exists. Works for every app, Syntica-hosted or GitHub-source. All access is confined to the repository of this application, on its deploy branch.

tools.name: app_repo_read_file
tools.description: Read one file of an application's code, on its deploy branch. Read a file before editing it, because a save replaces whole files. Works for every app, Syntica-hosted or GitHub-source. All access is confined to the repository of this application, on its deploy branch.

tools.name: app_repo_commit
tools.description: Save file changes into an application's code. All changes land together as one new version on the deploy branch. Each file REPLACES the file at its path in full (read it first to edit part of it), and deletes remove paths. On a Syntica-hosted app, saving updates the dev app automatically: the result carries a deployId, and you check progress with org_deploy_status. On a GitHub-source app the save goes to GitHub, and you run org_deploy afterwards to ship it. Saving never touches staging or production, which need org_deploy or org_promote. Repeat the userMessage of the result to the user. Tell the user their change is "saved" and that you are "updating your app", and call earlier states "versions", never say "commit". Works for every app, Syntica-hosted or GitHub-source. All access is confined to the repository of this application, on its deploy branch.

message.description: A short description of what changed, shown in the list of versions

files.description: Files to write. Each replaces the full file at its path (or creates it). Up to 100 changes per save.

content.description: The complete new file content (UTF-8 text; base64 with encoding: "base64")

encoding.description: How content is encoded (default utf-8; use base64 for binary files)

deletes.description: Repo-relative paths to delete in the same save

tools.name: app_list_versions
tools.description: List the saved versions of a Syntica-hosted application, newest first, with when each was saved, by whom and what changed. Use it when the user wants to go back to an earlier state, then pass a version id to app_restore_version. A GitHub-source app keeps its versions on GitHub, and this tool says so. Tell the user their change is "saved" and that you are "updating your app", and call earlier states "versions", never say "commit".

limit.description: How many versions to list (default 20, at most 100)

tools.name: app_restore_version
tools.description: Put back the files of an earlier version of a Syntica-hosted application, as a new save. Nothing is lost: the version it replaces stays in the list. Pass a versionId from app_list_versions, or leave it out to undo the last change. Like any save, it updates the dev app automatically: check progress with org_deploy_status and the deployId. Repeat the userMessage of the result to the user. Tell the user their change is "saved" and that you are "updating your app", and call earlier states "versions", never say "commit".

versionId.description: The version id from app_list_versions. Leave it out to undo the last change.

tools.name: org_get_action_policy
tools.description: Check what the organisation allows an AGENT to do in one application environment before proposing destructive work. Returns, per category (data_loss, availability, credentials), whether agents may act freely ("allow"), only with an administrator's token ("admin_only"), or not at all ("block"), and which scope that came from. Deleting production is admin-only by default. Read-only: the policy itself can only be changed by an administrator in the dashboard.

tools.name: app_list_node_tiers
tools.description: List the node tiers (instance sizes) available to an organisation, so the user can choose what an application's environment should run on. Returns the org's plan key alongside the tiers. On the Pay-as-you-go plan every tier is billed and the free tier is NOT selectable — always ask the user which tier to use rather than assuming one. On the free plan the free tier is the only option. Set the chosen tier with app_set_node_tier.

tools.name: app_set_node_tier
tools.description: Set which node tier (instance size) an application's environment runs on. Required before the first deploy of any environment on the Pay-as-you-go plan — org_deploy fails with NODE_TIER_REQUIRED until it is set, and must not be guessed: the tier determines what the customer is billed. Ask the user to choose from app_list_node_tiers first. On an already-provisioned environment the instance must be stopped first (app_stop_instance) — the change is then carried out on the infrastructure by app_reprovision_instance, after which the instance can be started again. Pass when "period_end" to schedule a downgrade for the 1st (or an ISO-8601 time before it) instead of now. The instance keeps its current size until then and nothing needs stopping. Only a downgrade can be scheduled. The reply lists paid slots that nothing uses, which can be reused until the 1st.

environment.description: Environment to set the tier for

when.description: 'now' (default), 'period_end' (the 1st 00:00 UTC) or an ISO-8601 time before the 1st

cloudAccount.description: Cloud account id or name from org_list_cloud_accounts. Optional, defaults to the Syntica hosted account. Only applies when this sets up the environment's first machine: an existing environment keeps its account. An own AWS account of the organisation is accepted once it is connected and its stack is current.

regionId.description: Deprecated, use cloudAccount. A region id is also a valid hosted account id.

tools.name: org_list_cloud_accounts
tools.description: List the cloud accounts an organisation can run environments in: the Syntica hosted account plus any AWS accounts the organisation connected. Returns id, name, provider, region, status, whether it is the default, its namespace (the name its environments get their default address under), updateRequired and placeable. Only an account with placeable true takes new environments. An own account becomes placeable once it is connected and its stack is recent enough. When a newer stack template is available, an account also carries updateUrl, the link that opens the stack update in the AWS console with the new template filled in, and whatChanges, one plain sentence per template version with what it unlocks. Updating is optional unless the organisation wants what it unlocks. A person applies it in the AWS console (review, tick the IAM acknowledgement, Submit). Syntica never updates the stack and this server cannot. An account that is still connecting (status pending) carries connection: the step it is at (linkOpened, stackStarted, networkCreated, roleCreated, verifying), its state, when it started, the stack link once known, and, when it failed or its link expired, why. A failed or expired connection is started again by an admin in the web app. Pass an id or name as cloudAccount to app_create, app_enable_environment or app_set_node_tier. Connecting or removing an account is done by an admin in the web app (Settings, Cloud accounts), never through this server. Needs cloud accounts to be enabled for the organisation. Without that, leave cloudAccount out and environments run on the Syntica hosted account.

tools.name: app_enable_environment
tools.description: Enable an environment for an application on the Pay-as-you-go plan. Staging and production are PAID, billed per application per month — calling this without confirm first returns the price so you can tell the user and get an explicit yes; only then call again with confirm: true. Never confirm on the user's behalf. Dev is free and included by default — this tool only needs it to RE-include a dev environment that was previously excluded on the Billing page. After enabling, the environment still needs a machine size before its first deploy: app_list_node_tiers, then app_set_node_tier. Optional cloudAccount (id or name from org_list_cloud_accounts) is checked before anything is enabled: the Syntica hosted account or one of the organisation's own connected AWS accounts. An own account whose stack needs an update is refused. Enabling does not place the environment. Pass the same cloudAccount to app_set_node_tier, which sets up its machine there. Left out, the environment runs on the Syntica hosted account.

applicationId.description: Application ID the environment belongs to

cloudAccount.description: Optional cloud account id or name from org_list_cloud_accounts: the Syntica hosted account or a connected own AWS account whose stack is current.

confirm.description: Required true for staging/production, and only after the user explicitly approved the monthly price returned by the unconfirmed call.

tools.name: app_list_custom_domains
tools.description: List the custom domains of an application environment with their state (PENDING_DNS while waiting for the DNS records, ACTIVE once serving), the DNS records to add, and lastError when something needs the user's attention. Each row carries `records`: the DNS records the user must add at their DNS provider, with type, name and value. A hosted environment needs one record: a CNAME to the platform ingress, or an A record for a root domain. An environment in the organisation's own AWS account needs two: a CNAME (purpose "routing") pointing the domain at the account's load balancer and a CNAME (purpose "validation") that lets AWS issue the certificate. That one must stay in place so the certificate renews. A root domain there gets an ALIAS record, which needs a DNS provider that supports ALIAS or CNAME flattening. Otherwise use a subdomain.

tools.name: app_add_custom_domain
tools.description: Add a custom domain (such as app.example.com) to an application environment. Returns the domain with the DNS records the user must add at their DNS provider. Tell the user exactly which records to add. Each row carries `records`: the DNS records the user must add at their DNS provider, with type, name and value. A hosted environment needs one record: a CNAME to the platform ingress, or an A record for a root domain. An environment in the organisation's own AWS account needs two: a CNAME (purpose "routing") pointing the domain at the account's load balancer and a CNAME (purpose "validation") that lets AWS issue the certificate. That one must stay in place so the certificate renews. A root domain there gets an ALIAS record, which needs a DNS provider that supports ALIAS or CNAME flattening. Otherwise use a subdomain. An environment in an own AWS account whose stack is too old, or whose account is disconnected, is refused with the reason.

environment.description: Environment to serve on the domain

hostname.description: The domain, for example app.example.com or example.com

tools.name: app_remove_custom_domain
tools.description: Remove a custom domain by its id (from app_list_custom_domains). The domain stops serving the app and its certificate is removed. Destructive: confirm with the user before calling. The user can then delete the DNS records they added.

tools.name: org_list_templates
tools.description: List all available project templates in the org template registry

tools.name: org_apply_template
tools.description: Overwrite an existing application repository with a fresh template scaffold. All existing code in the repository will be replaced.

appId.description: Application ID to apply the template to

templateId.description: ID of the template to apply (from org_list_templates)

tools.name: org_deploy
tools.description: Trigger a deployment for an application to a specified environment. Pass commitSha to ship a specific commit instead of the branch tip — this is how you roll back to a previous deployment. Returns a build ID to track progress with org_deploy_status.

commitSha.description: Specific commit SHA to deploy (7–40 hex chars). Defaults to the tip of `branch`. Use a sha from an earlier build to roll back.

tools.name: org_promote
tools.description: Promote the exact build currently running in one environment to another (e.g. staging → production). Ships the identical commit that succeeded in the source environment instead of re-resolving a branch tip, so the target matches what was tested. Returns a build ID to track with org_deploy_status.

fromEnvironment.description: Source environment to promote from (e.g. staging)

toEnvironment.description: Target environment to promote to (e.g. production)

tools.name: org_deploy_status
tools.description: Check how a deployment is going. Call it about every 10 seconds until stage is "live" or "failed". Stages in order: starting_machine, installing, building, live, failed. Relay each stage change to the user in plain words, using userMessage, and mention etaSeconds as a rough wait. When the stage is live, share the url. When it failed, tell the user the update did not finish, read failureReason, steps and logTail yourself to find the cause, and fix it before trying again. Say "updating your app" to the user.

tools.name: org_deploy_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a deployment that is currently running. Only works while the build is in the deploy phase; the build is marked failed with reason "Deployment cancelled by user".

tools.name: quality_get_status
tools.description: Get the latest SonarQube quality gate result for an application: whether the gate passed, how many findings are in new code, and when it last ran. Use before deploying to production when the app gates on quality, or when the user asks how the code is doing.

tools.name: quality_get_findings
tools.description: Get the findings from the latest SonarQube scan of an application, with file, line, rule and message for each. Use this to fix quality-gate failures: read the findings, change the code locally, then deploy. The analysis runs on the organisation's own SonarQube server.

tools.name: quality_trigger_scan
tools.description: Scan the application's current pushed head on the organisation's SonarQube server. Returns immediately; the scan runs in the background, so poll quality_get_status for the result. Use after pushing fixes for quality findings.

environment.description: Environment to attribute the scan to (default: dev)

tools.name: app_get_prevalidation_prompts
tools.description: Retrieve all pre-validation prompts for an application — the platform-standard set plus the organisation's own. Execute each prompt against the local code before committing.

tools.name: validation_get_generic_prompts
tools.description: Retrieve the standard, platform-wide security/validation prompts (the generic set, not tied to any application). Run each returned prompt against your staged diff before committing or deploying, and report its findings. Use this when the session is not tied to a specific application; use app_get_prevalidation_prompts when you have an applicationId and want the organisation's own prompts too.

tools.name: validation_list_prompts
tools.description: List the validation prompts visible to your organisation: the platform-standard set plus your org's own prompts (org / application / environment scope). Use this to see or manage what runs. Returns id, name, scope, and targeting for each.

tools.name: validation_add_prompt
tools.description: Add a custom validation prompt owned by your organisation, applied additively on top of the platform-standard prompts. Choose the scope: 'org' (all your apps), 'application' (one app — needs applicationId), or 'environment' (one env of one app — needs applicationId and environment). Write content as an instruction to the reviewing agent: what to look for, report each finding as ERROR or WARNING with file:line.

content.description: The check, written as an instruction for the reviewing agent

tools.name: validation_update_prompt
tools.description: Update the name and/or content of one of your organisation's own validation prompts. Cannot edit platform-standard prompts or another org's prompts.

tools.name: validation_delete_prompt
tools.description: Delete one of your organisation's own validation prompts by id. Cannot delete platform-standard prompts or another org's prompts.

tools.name: app_list_config
tools.description: List all config entries (values and secrets) visible for an application environment, across all scopes. Includes inherited entries from subscription, environment, and application scopes. Secret values are never returned.

tools.name: app_create_config
tools.description: Create a config entry for an application. kind="value" stores the value as plaintext (visible after creation). kind="secret" encrypts the value at rest — it cannot be retrieved after creation. Scope controls who inherits the entry: app_env (default), application, environment, or subscription. Subscription and environment scopes require org admin role.

applicationId.description: Application ID (used to identify the org for broad scopes)

scope.description: app_env (this app + environment only), application (all envs of this app), environment (all apps in this env), subscription (all apps in the org)

environment.description: Required when scope is app_env or environment

name.description: Entry key name (uppercase, underscores only — e.g. DATABASE_URL)

tools.name: app_delete_config
tools.description: Permanently delete a config entry by its ID.

tools.name: app_describe_connections
tools.description: Describe the platform connections granted to an application environment — mail, storage, databases, payments, AI and the rest of the connector catalogue. Returns each granted connection's connector, its name, and the environment variable NAMES the platform injects at deploy time. Never returns a credential. ALWAYS call this before writing or changing code that talks to an external system: write against the injected variables, never hardcode a credential, and never add a client library that contradicts the granted connector. If nothing is granted, say so and point the user at Connections rather than inventing a path of your own.

environment.description: Environment to describe — a grant in production does not imply one in dev

tools.name: app_request_connection
tools.description: Ask an organisation admin for a connection on one application environment. Use this when app_describe_connections returns nothing for the system you need — instead of asking the user for a credential or telling them to go and configure one. Names a connector from the catalogue (e.g. "smtp", "stripe", "slack"); the admin decides which of their connections satisfies it and is notified in the platform and by email. Repeating a request that is already pending returns the open one rather than queueing another.

environment.description: Environment the connection is needed in

connectorId.description: A connector id as returned by app_describe_connections, e.g. "smtp" or "stripe"

note.description: One line on what it is for — the admin reads this when deciding

tools.name: app_services_list
tools.description: List all running services for a deployed application in a given environment, with status, CPU and memory.

tools.name: app_service_start
tools.description: Start a specific service within a deployed application.

environment.description: Which environment: dev, staging or production

tools.name: app_service_stop
tools.description: Stop a specific service within a deployed application.

environment.description: Which environment: dev, staging or production

tools.name: app_service_restart
tools.description: Restart a specific service within a deployed application.

environment.description: Which environment: dev, staging or production

tools.name: app_service_logs
tools.description: Get the last N log lines from a service. Use this to debug crashes, startup errors, or runtime issues.

environment.description: Which environment: dev, staging or production

tail.description: Number of log lines to return (default 100)

tools.name: app_service_tail_logs
tools.description: Tail logs from a service, returning only lines newer than a previous call. Call repeatedly to follow live output. On the first call omit `since`; each response includes `nextSince` to pass to the next call.

environment.description: Which environment: dev, staging or production

since.description: Unix timestamp from a previous nextSince. Omit on first call.

tools.name: app_search_logs
tools.description: Search an application's RETAINED logs — including logs from containers that have since restarted, and from nodes that are stopped. Use this rather than app_service_logs when investigating something that already happened: "what did it say at 3am", "has this error appeared before", "what changed after the deploy". Matches a substring by default, or a regular expression with regex: true. Returns newest first.

query.description: Substring to match, or a regular expression when regex is true. Omit to return everything in the window.

regex.description: Treat query as a regular expression

minutes.description: How far back to search, in minutes. Defaults to 60.

limit.description: Maximum lines to return, up to 1000. Defaults to 200.

tools.name: app_recent_errors
tools.description: The most recent error lines from an application environment, across every service, from retained logs. Use this first when a user reports something is broken, when a deploy has just gone out, or before claiming an application is healthy. Matches common error markers (error, exception, fatal, traceback, unhandled) case-insensitively.

minutes.description: How far back to look, in minutes. Defaults to 60.

tools.name: app_health
tools.description: What the platform's uptime check last saw for each of an application's environments: up, down, asleep or unknown, since when, and the last error. Use before claiming an application is healthy, and when a user says "it is broken" — an environment reported asleep was stopped deliberately to save money and is not an outage.

tools.name: app_restart_instance
tools.description: Restart the EC2 instance for a deployed application. Performs a graceful stop (with automatic force-stop fallback if the instance does not respond) then starts it and brings containers up. Use this to recover from a stalled deployment.

tools.name: app_stop_instance
tools.description: Stop the EC2 instance for a deployed application environment. The application goes offline until it is started again; its data volume is kept. Required before changing the instance type with app_set_node_tier.

tools.name: app_start_instance
tools.description: Start the stopped EC2 instance for a deployed application environment and bring its containers up. Fails if the instance still runs a different size than the configured instance type — reprovision it with app_reprovision_instance first, or set the type back with app_set_node_tier.

tools.name: app_reprovision_instance
tools.description: Carry out a pending instance-type change on the infrastructure: resizes the stopped instance onto the type its node tier asks for, keeping the instance, its data volume, and its private IP. The instance must be stopped, and it is left stopped afterwards — start it with app_start_instance when the resize is done. Use this after app_set_node_tier when starting the instance is refused for a type mismatch.

tools.name: app_replace_instance
tools.description: DESTRUCTIVE. Destroy an environment's EC2 instance and its volumes, then reset the node so the next deploy builds a fresh one from the current infrastructure template. ALL DATA IN THAT ENVIRONMENT IS LOST — the instance's volumes go with it. Custom domains, the ingress policy, backup records, environment config and the application URL are all preserved. Use this for a node too old to be fixed in place, for example one provisioned before the dedicated data volume existed, whose backups therefore cannot work. Unlike app_reprovision_instance (which only resizes and keeps everything) this replaces the machine outright. After it completes, deploy to provision the replacement.

confirm.description: Must be true. Acknowledges that all data in this environment will be destroyed.

tools.name: app_dev_sync
tools.description: Sync the instance to the latest pushed code and rebuild/restart specific Docker Compose services, skipping infrastructure provisioning. Waits up to 40s; fast syncs return their final result (including the build log) directly. If the sync is still running after that, a build ID is returned — poll org_deploy_status until status is "success" or "failed". Only works on environments where dev sync is enabled (default: enabled on dev, disabled on staging and production). Use for fast development iteration after pushing code changes.

services.description: Docker Compose service names to restart after git pull (e.g. ["api", "worker"])

tools.name: app_db_query
tools.description: Run a SQL query against a deployed application's database. Read-only by default. Set allowWrite:true only for intentional mutations (e.g. seeding a first admin account); confirm with the user first. Returns CSV text (capped at 1000 rows). Every query is audit-logged.

service.description: Database service name (from docker-compose, e.g. "db" or "postgres")

tools.name: app_db_audit
tools.description: List recent database-query audit entries for a deployed application (who ran what, newest first).

environment.description: Which environment: dev, staging or production
